page.layout: One printed page, single text block with a heading above it. Heading "ARTICULUS V." with its title, then one paragraph of running text in full measure. No marginal notes. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.l: ARTICULUS V.
Picolominæus cap. 25. de placitis veterum philo-
sophorum, confiderandum eft, inquit, putasse

l.i: nonnullos in universo cœlum quiescere, & terram re-
volvi, in qua nos constituti, & cum ea revoluti pu-
tamus revolvi cœlum, ex horum numero fuerunt He-
raclides Ponticus, referente Simplicio in secundo de
Cœlo 53. nec non Philolaus Pythagoreus, Ecphantes
rente Cicerone in Academicis & afferente, Theophra-
stum id retulisse. Plutarchus etiam in septima quastio-
ne Platonica, inquit, Aristarchum, & Selencum id

main_text.l: ipsum existimasse. Hi autem in duas series divisi
erant, nonnulli enim putarunt terram in medio uni-
versi esse collocatam, in eoque revolvi, quod Aristo-
teles tribuit Platoni in secundo de Cœlo 76. & ex re-
centioribus Copernicus id ipsum tuetur. Et hæc Pico-
lominæus. Hæc sententia, licet Platonis fuisse non
putem, si absurda est: non tamen ex parte terræ aut
cœlorum ullam patitur incongruitatem. Quod
namque molem terream & ab aëre dejectam[?]& seipsa
deorsum tendentem difficulter volubilem videamus,
non infert terram in suo loco sitam, nec jam alio la-
tam, nec ab ullo cohibitam non posse circulariter fer-
ri & quidem motu velocissimo. Neque si ita move-
retur sentiremus; ut qui in flumine vehitur navi quæ
nullam jactationem excipiat non sentit se moveri,
potestque per eam incedere: & si in ripam oculos
conjiciet

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "Selencum" (probably Seleucum as printed, kept as seen); "dejectam& seipsa" marked [?] at dejectam. The heading title may be set with a ligature in cœlorum; read as cælorum. Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Text ends with "ripam oculos"; "conjiciet" is the catchword.
